AutoGluon.Installation: Python package with all optional components (`autogluon.tabular[all]`), tested with Python 3.11. Large environment of about 1.8 GB. On macOS, the OpenMP library is required for its LightGBM models. Running AutoGluon without it was not tested. Set `num_gpus=0` to enforce CPU-only training.
AutoGluon.Data preparation: None required. The raw table can be passed to the tool.
AutoGluon.Settings: Tested with the preset `best_quality` instead of the default `medium_quality`. The metric of the search can be set with `eval_metric`.
AutoGluon.Resource use: Used the full time budget. Memory peaks of up to about 14 GB.

Problems and warnings.general: A dependency interaction caused a pandas prediction error in the tested macOS setup: the fastai library sets the pandas option `mode.chained_assignment` to raise an error. Resetting it to `warn` before predicting resolved the error.
Problems and warnings.classification: For multiclass tasks, check whether rare classes are retained: in the tested setup, classes with fewer than ten training examples could be removed and would then never be predicted. Consider adjusting `label_count_threshold` (passed in `learner_kwargs`) if necessary.

AutoGluon.Documentation: `auto.gluon.ai`, including a cheat sheet and a quick start for tabular data.

auto-sklearn.Version and licence: auto-sklearn 0.15.0, BSD 3-Clause Licence. No release since 2022.
auto-sklearn.Installation: Officially supports Linux only. Its memory limit relies on resource limits of the Linux kernel, which macOS does not enforce, so on macOS the tool can use up the entire memory. On macOS and Windows, a Linux container is recommended. Python 3.10 was used. The macOS installation required building scikit-learn 0.24 from source with additional build tools, together with older versions of NumPy, SciPy, and pandas. Use the supplied environment pins to reproduce this setup.
auto-sklearn.Data preparation: Categorical columns must be converted to the pandas `category` type, as text columns are otherwise treated as free text rather than as categorical.
auto-sklearn.Settings: Default search configuration. Only the runtime, resources, seed, and metric were set. The metric of the search can be set with `metric`. The memory limit per worker (`memory_limit`) should be adjusted to the available memory.
auto-sklearn.Resource use: Used the full time budget. Memory peaks of up to about 13 GB.
auto-sklearn.Problems and warnings: No tool-specific problems in the benchmark runs beyond those common to all tools.

FLAML.Installation: Python package (`flaml[automl]`), tested with Python 3.11. On macOS, the OpenMP library has to be installed separately, as the tool failed without it.
FLAML.Data preparation: None required. The raw table can be passed to the tool.
FLAML.Settings: Default search configuration. Only the runtime, resources, seed, and metric were set. The metric of the search can be set with `metric`.
FLAML.Resource use: Used the full time budget. Median memory below 1 GB, with peaks of up to about 15 GB.
FLAML.Problems and warnings: No tool-specific problems in the benchmark runs beyond those common to all tools.

H2O AutoML.Installation: Python package, tested with Python 3.11. Requires a Java runtime, as the tool runs as a local Java server. The packages `numpy` and `pandas` have to be installed separately.

Data preparation.general: Categorical columns should be declared as categorical (`enum`), as the tool chooses the column types itself unless they are declared and may read categories stored as numbers as numeric values.
Data preparation.classification: Declare the target as categorical as well.

H2O AutoML.Settings: Default search configuration. Only the runtime, resources, seed, and metric were set. The metric for ranking the models can be set with `sort_metric`, but macro-F1 is not available. The Java heap limit (`max_mem_size`) should leave memory available for the Python client and, where XGBoost is available, for XGBoost, which runs outside the Java heap. H2O recommends giving the heap at most two thirds of the available memory.
H2O AutoML.Resource use: Used the full time budget. Memory peaks of up to about 15 GB.
H2O AutoML.Problems and warnings: XGBoost is not supported on Windows or on the Apple M1 chip according to the documentation, and it was not available on the tested Apple M4 Pro either, natively or in Linux containers. The tool then searches without XGBoost models, which can be checked with `H2OXGBoostEstimator.available()`. The tool removed constant columns on its own, without stopping the run.
H2O AutoML.Documentation: `docs.h2o.ai`, AutoML section of the user guide.

LightAutoML.Installation: Python package, tested with Python 3.11. Installation took about 15 minutes. On macOS, training stopped responding in the tested setup, so a Linux container is recommended.

Data preparation.classification: The predicted class probabilities have to be mapped to the class labels with the tool's class mapping.

LightAutoML.Settings: Default preset (`TabularAutoML`). The metric can be set when defining the task (`Task`).
LightAutoML.Resource use: Usually finished well before the time budget. Memory peaks of up to about 5 GB.

Problems and warnings.classification: Check the distribution of predicted classes and compare performance with a majority-class baseline. Majority-only predictions occurred in a tested task with substantial missingness, many predictors, and severe class imbalance, although these characteristics were not established as the cause.

Lightwood.Installation: Python package, tested with Python 3.11. Needs language data (NLTK) when it treats a column as text and downloads them if missing, which requires internet access unless the data are installed beforehand.

Data preparation.classification: Declare the target type, as class labels stored as numbers can otherwise be treated as a numeric target.

Lightwood.Settings: Default settings, including its default metrics balanced accuracy and R². Other metrics can be specified in the model specification.
Lightwood.Resource use: Usually finished well before the time budget. Memory peaks of up to about 3 GB.

Problems and warnings.general: Inspect inferred column types and retained predictors, because the tool automatically removes columns that it classifies as identifiers or as uninformative.
Problems and warnings.classification: Compare performance with a majority-class baseline: the tool scored below that baseline in one tested task. This observation does not establish a general effect of missingness or dimensionality.

MLJAR AutoML.Installation: Python package, tested with Python 3.11. The first import after installation was slow.

Data preparation.general: None required for regression and multiclass tasks.
Data preparation.classification: In binary tasks with the tested `Compete` configuration, encode the labels as 0 and 1 and map predictions back to the original labels, which avoided a stacking-related prediction failure.

MLJAR AutoML.Settings: Tested in mode `Compete` instead of the default `Explain`. The metric of the search can be set with `eval_metric`. Writes a report with a leaderboard and explanations for each run.
MLJAR AutoML.Resource use: Used the full time budget, sometimes slightly more. Memory peaks of up to about 6 GB.
MLJAR AutoML.Problems and warnings: For tables with more than 10,000 rows, consider AutoGluon as an alternative: MLJAR AutoML ranked significantly lower on the tested datasets with more than 10,000 rows. This does not establish which tool will perform best on a new table. Its feature selection removed predictors that it judged uninformative.

TPOT.Version and licence: TPOT 1.1.0, GNU Lesser General Public License 3.0.
TPOT.Installation: Python package, tested with Python 3.11. The tested installation required an older `setuptools` version because a dependency used `pkg_resources`. The installed version 1.x has a different interface from version 0.x, to which many online examples still refer.

Data preparation.general: The built-in preprocessing (`preprocessing=True`) should be enabled, and columns entirely missing in the training data should be removed.
Data preparation.classification: In the tested `TPOTClassifier` wrapper, text class labels were returned as encoded numbers and had to be decoded with `label_encoder_`.

TPOT.Settings: Default search configuration. Only the runtime, resources, seed, and metric were set. The time limit is set in minutes (`max_time_mins`), and the metric of the search with `scorers`.
TPOT.Resource use: Often exceeded the time limit, by up to about 65%. Memory peaks of up to about 30 GB.
TPOT.Problems and warnings: Allow time beyond the optimisation budget, as total fit time exceeded the configured limit in the tests. Monitor memory when using parallel workers: in one observed run, the workers reached about 30 GB of the 32 GB limit and two processes were stopped by the operating system. Reducing `n_jobs` may reduce memory pressure, but this mitigation was not tested.
